findings.passage: “It’s a solution in search of a problem,” Johnson said. “Look, nobody can point to me one issue of voter fraud in Mississippi that is raised to the level of needing a law. None. I can’t even think of one.”
findings.note: Quoted by Mississippi Public Broadcasting on SB 2588 (SHIELD Act: citizenship check at registration and annual check of the voter roll). Date is the article date (page shows March 25 and an update March 26, 2026); the day he spoke is not stated.
subjects: SHIELD Act citizenship checks of voter rolls

findings.passage: “There’s a section in here that says a registered voter who has failed to vote at least once in any election, or update his registration during a period that begins in a presidential preference, you put all of these requirements on a person that’s registered to vote,” Johnson said.
findings.note: Quoted by Magnolia Tribune (article date) in House debate on the conference report for HB 1310 (2023), arguing against its rule on voters who do not vote or update their registration. Voter-roll item, not an ID rule.

findings.passage: “In this day, two days after a whole town got wiped out, we’re getting ready to make a whole town, a whole county, inactive cause they’re not going to vote. For what?” Johnson said.
findings.note: Quoted by Magnolia Tribune (article date) in the same HB 1310 (2023) debate, after a tornado had destroyed a town; objects to making voters inactive for not voting.
